meg-ale: Oh, you're brand new. Okay. People call it the Backrooms. All of it. This floor is Level 1, the yellow carpet you crawled out of is Level 0, and it keeps going down from there.
Nobody knows. It's like a parking garage somebody forgot to finish. Each floor's a different kind of wrong. We number them so we can complain properly.
Dina. Yeah, maybe. Quiet one, kept asking which stairs go where. I told her down is the only direction that works. Callum would have her written down. He writes everybody down.
Callum's cans. I know it's you, Ale. Why?
No idea what you're talking about. Go count something.
Put them back or I tell Callum and he tells the M.E.G.
Tell him. He'll ask you where your proof is, and you'll have nothing. Walk.
Take two bottles of my almond water. Help me find a way to keep that family fed.
Two bottles. They'll last the kids a few days. It's a family out east. Callum won't like it, but maybe he'll listen to you.
meg-callum: Ortiz needs purification tablets. She says you've got a tin.
That tin is for emergencies. Fill out a form. We don't have forms. So, no.
Bad water means sick runners, and sick runners eat your rations lying down.
Fifteen Backdollars for the tin. Paperwork can wait.
Fifteen? That tin's worth more than you.
Pockets where I can see them on your way out.
Camp stores, Level 1. Folk call the lot of it the Backrooms. I just call it the job. What I know is what's on these shelves and who's in this book.
Ortiz needs purification tablets. She says you've got a tin.
That tin is for emergencies. Fill out a form. We don't have forms. So, no.
meg-ortiz: Sit. You are swaying. No, do not say you are fine, everyone says that. Hands out, let me see.
You look worried, doc. What's going on?
Runner came in drinking from the dark puddles. Fever, shakes. I need purification tablets and Callum sits on the only tin like it's gold. Get it from him. However you get it.
Callum's rations are going missing. Seen anyone eating better than they should?
I dressed a cut on Ale's palm yesterday. She said she caught it on a door. Looked like she'd pulled the lid off a tin.
Look at me. Eyes. Good. Hands. Good enough.
My head's not right. What do I do?
First, do not tell people your head is not right. Second, drink this. Third, lie down.
hold still. there. you're good to walk.
surv-mags: Well, look at this. Hi, honey. You buying, selling, or window shopping? Window's free. For now.
Mags's. Finest store between that boiler and that other boiler. You want the big picture, ask Hollis. I do retail.
Honey, if there was an out I'd be selling tickets at the door. There's no out. There's just deeper, and a few spots that are nicer than others. This is one of the nicer ones. Sad, right?
The one with the tape recorder. Sure. Traded me a real nice wristwatch for rubber boots and didn't even argue. You only want rubber boots for one place, honey. The barred door.
surv-wren: Stop! Stay there. Turn so I can see your face. Okay. You've got one. Sorry, new person. Had to check.
Out of the pipes? Stairs up, or the barred door. Out of everything? I don't know. I stopped asking. Mags says there's no out, Hollis says the radio comes from somewhere. Pick one.
The tape lady? She talked into a little box the whole time, like it was a friend. She let me say hi into it. She went off toward the hot pipes. I told her not to.
surv-hollis: Easy there, neighbor. Put the bag down, it's safe. Mags might peek in it. Nobody else will.
Hiss, mostly. Some nights a fella reads out numbers. One night a woman sang a whole lullaby. I took down the words. Couldn't tell you what tongue it is.
Only comes at night. And only once you've quit waiting on it.
Dina. I do. Sat right there two nights with her ear on my radio and a little tape machine running. Said that signal sounded like home. Then she packed up and went through the barred door.
gamma-reyes: Dina. One night at the gate, months back. She had a hand-drawn map with doors marked on it. Good work, better than ours. She asked my patrol about a hotel. I told her that is a campfire story.
Electrical station. Level 3 on our maps. Miles of halls, live cable, and machines nobody switched on. My part of it is this gate and one lap around it.
Dina. One night at the gate, months back. She had a hand-drawn map with doors marked on it. Good work, better than ours. She asked my patrol about a hotel. I told her that is a campfire story.
My orders are to hold a gate, not find a door home. Command says the scouts are working on it. Command has said that the whole time I have been here.
gamma-ito: Sit. Water is boiling. You have not slept, I can see it. The hum does that to new faces.
In the sick room of a base, inside a power station that powers nothing. That is the honest answer. The others will give you a number. The number does not help you sleep.
I do not know. I know what happens to the ones who think about it all day. They stop eating, then they walk toward the big cables. So think about it a little. Then eat.

Yes. She did not hum. She kept one earphone in, listening to her own voice on a tape. Clever. I asked what she recorded. She said every door she found, so the next person would not start from nothing.
hold still. there. you're good to walk.
gamma-tess: Mm. That jacket. Who made this seam? No. Do not say. I will only suffer.
gamma-pell: Name for the ledger, please. None? Then you are 'Visitor', underlined. What have you brought to trade?
two almond waters and a ration. don't waste them.
l5-odette: Mm. You are dripping on my carpet, new one. Stay out of the ballroom. I do not clean in there.
homely-barnaby: two almond waters and a ration. don't waste them.
A pleasure to see you again. Truly.
Sit, my dear guest. A hot towel. A cup of something. A minute's quiet. There. We look after our guests. We always look after our guests.
Sit, my dear guest. A hot towel. A cup of something. A minute's quiet. There. We look after our guests. We always look after our guests.
The front hall of the Homely Hotel, my dear guest. I hold this door. It is nineteen thirty-one, the weather is mild, and you are most welcome.
The front hall of the Homely Hotel, my dear guest. I hold this door. It is nineteen thirty-one, the weather is mild, and you are most welcome.
I am poor with names and good with luggage. A lady went out through my door with one bag, quite early. She said 'the city', and I said 'which one', and she said that was a fair question.
l5-samantha: Sit. I was expecting you. Not hoping. Expecting.
Empty paws, cara? My saucer is empty too. I read for supper. Bring me meat and sit.
You are asking a cat how doors work. We sit in front of them until somebody opens one. It has never failed me. It may take you longer.
You came back, visitor. I knew you would. I know a great many things.
Ah. You smell of supper. Set it down, mon cher, and I will tell you what is coming.
Bene. Sit. Let me look at you.
Empty paws, cara? My saucer is empty too. I read for supper. Bring me meat and sit.

You should search the Coat check here in The Beverly Room first; its battery and pistol rounds may serve you better than haste. In the Suite, a Bobby pin can turn the Writing desk’s stubborn lock, and the Royal ration and Almond water within will ease your hunger and thirst; the Vanity holds duct tape for what is fraying. Avoid the Boiler Room—the hound there is no mere rumor—and seek Imani at the M.E.G. Outpost “Housekeeping” if you need a steadier ally. Your clearest way out is the Old Stairway up to Level 4; the sealed doors promise nothing, mon cher. You came here from the levels above, and the hotel remembers each time it watched you die.
l5-ambrose: Good evening, guest, and welcome to the Homely Hotel. We were expecting you. We are always expecting someone.
Certainly. Fifteen for a room, forty for a suite. Every one overlooks the corridor. Ring the bell and I shall see to your key.
l5-harlan: Quartermaster. Ammo, bandages, one submachine gun. None of it cheap, buyer. I keep the count in my head. Don't try me on it.
A hotel. Staff run the upstairs. My lot hold the basement side and keep the vermin down. We call ourselves Housekeeping. It's a joke. Nobody laughs.
Don't know one. I know ways off this floor of the world, and every one of them is worse than a warm bed here. People work that out and stay. Then they buy from me.
Rounds still cost what they cost.
l5-vanderholt: In a hotel I do not own. I have made three offers. The man at the desk says it is not for sale. Everything is for sale, upstart. That is what frightens me about this place.
One buys one's way out of anything. I simply have not found who to pay. When I do, I shall go first, and you may apply to my secretary.
Four thousand miles of steel. I put towns where there was only dust. Now I cannot buy one hotel. It is galling.

I do not retain the names of debtors, there are too many. A young woman from the third floor borrowed forty from me for a fare. A fare to where, I asked. 'The city, and then a boat.' Nobody in this hotel has ever repaid me. She left an envelope at the desk with forty in it. I was quite upset.
You bargain like a railwayman. Very well. A steal. I shall tell the club you robbed me.
Cornelius Vanderholt knocks 15% off for you
homely-auguste: AH! Mon ami! You look starved. Auguste will fix this. Sit! No, there! Sit!
Mon ami is back! Sit, eat!
Then you found the right kitchen! Broth, bread, meat. Slowly. No, faster. There. You live. I am a genius.
l5-dolores: You! Skinny! Sit. Steak, chicken, or stew. You pick, or I pick, and I always pick stew.
l02-capn: Ah. A visitor. Mind the carpet, it is new. Everything is new. Sorry for the inconvenience.

Remodeling. It is going great. Mostly. The rooms back there keep rearranging themselves when nobody looks, and my crew left three cans of the good paint somewhere inside. Keep a work lamp on a wall and it stays put. Bring the paint out and I will make it worth your while.
l5-beast: Welcome, guest. May I help you find your room?
Lovely. Look at all these names. Now, one small courtesy: this card goes under the door of Room 1408. Don't knock. Don't read it. Just slide it under and walk away.
Tobias. The clerk. He's late on something he owes me. Nothing for you to worry about.
Welcome, guest. May I help you find your room?
The card's under the door of 1408.
There. I'm a man of my word. The hotel won't trouble you anymore, not the halls, not the hum. Come and go as you please. I'll be watching. Fondly.
Put Tobias's debt on my tab. [$200]
Paid in full. How touching. Tell the clerk he can sleep tonight. Tell him I said goodnight.
l5-tobias: Oh! New person. Hi. There's a job on the board, five rats, pays in water. Can we talk over here? Not by the vent. Over here.
You look like you've seen a ghost.
Worse. Look. This came under my door. His card. Blank on both sides, but I know what it means. Did you put it there?
Right. Sure. Then it just walked in. Either way, you're the only one here he talks to. Ask him to let it go. Please.
Oh, new person! Rats! I mean hi!
You're free. He's done with you.
Free. Huh. I'm gonna sleep with the lights off. No I'm not. Here, it's my whole tip jar. Don't argue. And if you ever need a room fast, my door's open.
You want the job? Or just a chat. A chat's fine. I can chat.
hub-meg-lin: Thirty-two hooks. Thirty-one keys. I counted at lights-down and I counted again and one walked. Nobody signed for it. If you want to be useful, that's how.
two almond waters and a ration. don't waste them.
You again. Sign the sheet if you're drawing, don't if you're not.
Fine. Dace had the late watch. Start there. And visitor, if you find it, it comes back to this desk. Not to your pocket.
Try it. Dace bent six picks and a butter knife. There's nothing inside to pick. It's a hole that wants one thing.
hub-meg-sato: Oh. A walker. Don't stand on the chalk, please, that's four days of work you're about to stand on.

We found more road. Past the barrier, where the lamps stop. A team of three went in with survey recorders and came out without them, running. The reports say 'equipment abandoned'. I'd give a great deal to hear those tapes.
l11-walker-1: Coming through, chief! Got a parcel for across town? Give me the address. I beat most of the lights.
That's a lot of parcels. Need a hand with a Sedco manifest?

Sedco's night alarm tripped on camera four and time-locked the shop and its vault, with a week of my signed manifests inside. Get into the terminal out front, blind camera four, and pull the master drive from the vault under 14th Street. We split the cash. You in, chief?

Okay, here's the deal, chief. Sedco's night alarm tripped on camera four and the whole shop time-locked, vault and all, with a week of my signed manifests inside. No manifests, no pay. Get in, blind camera four so it doesn't trip again, and pull the master drive from the vault under 14th Street. Whatever cash is down there, we split it down the middle.
Got it. The master security drive, out of the vault.
That's the one. Under the parcels it goes. Seventy-five, your half, and the two kits I swiped off the depot shelf. If management asks, I ran the route myself.
l11-meg-agent-vance: Easy, citizen. Specialist Vance. I walk this street by day and sit the radio set by night. Things are polite in this city. Don't let it relax you.
l61-sal: Grab a stool, kid. Burgers are on and the fryer just came up to heat.
I know orders, kid, not names. Ask the helpers by the fryer. They keep a board of who's looking for who.
l61-amber-b: Somebody fed me when I was new and didn't ask for a thing. Jo in The Hub runs the real infirmary, and Pip holds the chalk routes; we just keep the warm bench open on this end.

Oh, sweetie. Sit down first. People call this the Snackrooms—Level 6.1. Sal keeps the grill warm and the Facelings bus every tray so fast it spooks newcomers, but you're safe at this table, I promise that much.

East glass doors step straight out onto Level 11 concrete, and Pip's chalk runners know how to fold back into The Hub from there. Just mind the Guild pilgrims if you take the metal vent—that drops straight into Level 3.

Let me think. There's a card on the board. 'DINA, if you read this, wait here.' No one signed it, and Bee swore she saw a woman matching that tread headed toward the Guild's red-chalk corner. It's been up a long time, sweetie.
l61-patron-e: Hold up. Stand under the light where I can see you.
Somewhere behind everything. That's my best guess. I was in a parking garage, then I wasn't. You'll want somebody smarter than me.
l61-amber-a: Hi, sweetie! We're Camp Amber—Wren at the Annex board. We help people get settled at The Hub, or find who stepped off the wrong bus. Water? A blanket? A look at the board?
That board mentions someone named Bee in a red coat.

Her partner left that notice three sleeps back — bright red coat, came off the 8:15 bus route through the glass doors into Level 11, then nothing. Search the 11th Avenue crossing out there, follow any lead through the tunnels to our camp in The Hub, and bring me word she's alive. Can you walk that far, sweetie?

Her partner pinned that card three sleeps back. Bright red wool coat, tall, came off the 8:15 bus route out through the glass doors onto 11th Avenue. Nobody's seen her since. Check the crossing bench out there, or ask the commuters, then bring word straight back here.
l61-guild-a: Many of us, many paths, one road. The Guild of Many welcomes you, traveller. Have you counted the seams between this booth and Level 3?
l61-guild-b: Many of us, many paths, one road. The Guild of Many welcomes you, traveller. Have you counted the seams between this booth and Level 3?

Pilgrims and barge-clerks. Our main ledger hangs in Level 11's old wharf district—where Kael runs his crane—and our runners log every grate from Level 3 up to the Level 4 vending wall. One day the Book of Ways is whole, and somebody reads the way home in it.

On a braided seam, traveller. Level 6.1 feeds the hungry, yet its grease-traps bleed straight into Level 3's electrical tunnels and our old redoubt plate under the duct, and a stray coin in Level 4's B4 dispenser still drops you back on these tiles.
Four hundred and twelve ways are inked in the Book—some into Level 11, some down the east vent into Level 3, one back up a lift to Level 4's office block. None is labeled 'home'. Wait for Page 413.

A woman copied pages from our Book and gave the name Dina. She copied only the ways marked 'unsure'—especially the three-way seam linking Level 6.1, Level 3, and Level 4. We thought it a strange choice.

the-way-back.name: The Way Back
the-way-back.step: Dina left the hotel for a city, looking for a radio. Find the city and ask who ran one for her.
history: Find a way out of the yellow rooms. Look for someone who knows a route home.
Something left you a name: Dina. Find people. Ask where you are, and who she is.
Find out who Dina is. Somebody at the camp keeps a list of names.
Dina asked about ways out, then went down. Look for what she left on the levels below the camp.
Dina's tape says she took a room at the hotel on Level 5. Ask the staff what she left behind.
Dina's tape says she took a room at a hotel, a few levels down. Find it and ask the staff what she left behind.

bad-water.name: Bad Water
bad-water.step: Get purification tablets out of Callum for Dr. Ortiz

err-tess-sweep.step: Check in with Duke on watch
history: Deal with what's scratching at the walls: 0 / 4
Deal with what's scratching at the walls: 1 / 4

Deal with what's scratching at the walls: 3 / 4

err-harlan-ledger.name: The Guest Book
err-harlan-ledger.step: Bring Harlan a whiskey for his trouble
history: Ask Vanderholt about the guest book
Find the bar cart in the ballroom

the-tenth-tunnel.name: The Tenth Tunnel
the-tenth-tunnel.step: Take the door in the tenth tunnel.
history: Phoebe says the M.E.G. post in these tunnels writes down everyone who passes. Ask at Doorstep Carpet if Dina came through.
Ask at the M.E.G. post, Doorstep Carpet, if Dina came through.

hub-missing-key.name: The Missing Key
hub-missing-key.step: A Level Key left Lin's cabinet unsigned. Ask Dace at the barrier who came through on his watch.

the-dead-signal.name: The Dead Signal
the-dead-signal.step: Run. Keep your balance over the gurneys and outrun the corridor collapse down to the EXIT sign.
the-dead-signal.briefing: Chapter 2: Dina's trail through Level 11's clinic and Base Gamma's archive leads to an unstable hospital anomaly behind the strip mall.

errand-l61-tray.name: Bus Your Tray
errand-l61-tray.step: Finish your food, then slide the tray into the tray return rack in the Level 6.1 food court. Sal at Burger Bop and the facelings notice who cleans up.

coat-of-red-bus-to-nowhere.name: Coat of Red, Bus to Nowhere
coat-of-red-bus-to-nowhere.step: Search the 11th Avenue crossing bus bench in Level 11 for traces of Bee's red coat, or ask the commuters nearby.
coat-of-red-bus-to-nowhere.briefing: Wren at Camp Amber is looking for Bee, last seen wearing a red coat off Level 11's 8:15 bus route. Search the 11th Avenue crossing in Level 11, follow her trail to Camp Amber in The Hub (Jo or Pip), and bring word back to Wren in Level 6.1.

short-rations.name: Short Rations
short-rations.text: Quest completed: Short Rations · Callum's Lucky Thirteen
history: Find out who's been taking cans from Callum's crates
Ale's been eating well. Deal with her

the-gentleman-s-terms.name: The Gentleman's Terms
the-gentleman-s-terms.text: You kept your end. The hotel stopped pressing on you. Something in the portraits keeps watching.
history: Bring the Gentleman the guest register from the front desk
Slip his calling card under the door of Room 1408

tobias-s-debt.name: Tobias's Debt
tobias-s-debt.text: Tobias tore the card in half and laughed for the first time since you met him.
history: Get the Gentleman to let Tobias off his debt

spotlight-on-sedco.name: Spotlight on Sedco
spotlight-on-sedco.text: Quest Completed: Spotlight on Sedco · Split the vault with the courier (+120 XP, +$75.00)
history: Get into terminal SEDCO-SEC-01 on the desk outside Sedco Spotlight (log in, or hack it), then release the front door from its security panel.
Inside Sedco, search the sales counter and review the camera feeds on the monitor wall.
Review the camera feeds on Sedco's monitor wall.
Reset the stage spotlight in the corner of the shop. Camera four is blind while it points at the lens.
Open the Sedco crate in the vault under the 14th Street subway station and take the master drive.
spotlight-on-sedco.briefing: The courier's manifests are locked in Sedco Spotlight's vault. Get into terminal SEDCO-SEC-01 (log in or hack it; the courier may know the password [Speech 30]), blind camera four with the stage spotlight, and bring back the master drive from under 14th Street. Vance at Base Beta wants the drive too.

errand-l61-tray.name: Bus Your Tray
errand-l61-tray.text: Returned the tray to the rack. The nearest faceling nodded at you. (+3 XP, +3 Sanity)

quest.name: Coat of Red, Bus to Nowhere
quest.step: Search the 11th Avenue crossing bus bench in Level 11 for traces of Bee's red coat, or ask the commuters nearby.
